summary: Practise cost-effectiveness and budget impact analysis for health decisions. Explore the course and build decision-ready economic evidence.
lede: Health technology assessment uses economic evaluation to compare health interventions for resource decisions. Designed for health economists, programme managers and policy analysts, the course covers framing evaluations, comparing costs and outcomes, calculating an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio, testing uncertainty, estimating budget impact and communicating assumptions, affordability and limitations in decision briefs.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess health interventions, prepare programme budgets, or advise payers on prioritisation and coverage using economic evidence. This course is designed for: Ministry of health planners prioritising interventions across programme budgets. Health economists comparing intervention costs, outcomes, and uncertainty. Public-health programme managers assessing the affordability of service changes. Health insurer analysts reviewing evidence for benefit-package decisions. Donor health advisers comparing proposed programme options and resource needs. Health policy analysts preparing economic evidence for coverage recommendations. HTA analysts documenting comparators, assumptions, and evidence limitations. Health financing specialists reviewing budget impact estimates for payers. Clinical programme leads defining populations and comparators for evaluations. Research organisation analysts translating evaluation findings into decision briefs.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with health programmes, payer decisions, or programme budgeting is recommended. Basic numeracy and comfort reviewing tables or spreadsheets will help; coding or programming is not required.
